meta.title: Mr. Barker Goes to Washington
meta.subtitle: A Satirical Congress Micro-Sim
meta.worldNote: Everyone in Maple Creek and Washington can be any animal—teachers, bakers, librarians, and lawmakers alike. The Capitol power brokers you collide with just happen to lean into classic literary fables, while every bill satirizes purely how Congress functions.

artDirection.description: Crisp flat-graphic editorial print aesthetic inspired by Aviary Attorney: warm parchment paper, thick charcoal ink outlines, flat block shading, subtle newspaper halftones, bold congressional crimson, navy, brass gold, and ink black.

barker.name: Rep. Barnaby Barker
barker.visualBrief: Earnest golden-tan floppy-eared freshman puppy in a slightly oversized off-the-rack navy suit, polka-dot bow tie, perked hopeful ears (droop when stressed).

rolodex.whatTheyWant: Survive a 10-week freshman term, pass a signature Flagship Bill, and win reelection in Maple Creek.
rolodex.watchOut: You can't keep 100% of Families, Seniors, Main Street, Leadership, and Donors happy at once—pick your coalition.

sheep.name: Martha Ewe
sheep.visualBrief: No-nonsense community organizer with curly cream wool, round brass spectacles, forest-green knit cardigan, holding a town-hall clipboard.

rolodex.whatTheyWant: Clean, transparent bills that deliver for everyday hometown voters without hidden traps.
rolodex.watchOut: When a bill splits Families, Seniors, and Main Street, even Martha looks conflicted—read your postcards and Toby's memo!

wolf.name: Whip Fenrir Fang
wolf.visualBrief: Razor-sharp slate-gray wolf in a crisp charcoal pinstripe suit, crimson power tie, brass monocle, gleaming whip-count clipboard.

rolodex.whatTheyWant: Strict Caucus loyalty on leadership bills and must-pass omnibuses—no surprise defections.
rolodex.watchOut: Sink into Backbench Exile and he'll freeze your Week 6 Flagship Bill (forcing 4 votes instead of 3). Never break a handshake promise.

snake.name: Vesper Viper, Esq.
snake.visualBrief: Sleek emerald viper in a tailored brocade waistcoat, gold pocket-watch chain, tinted pince-nez glasses, calm unblinking poise.

rolodex.whatTheyWant: Favorable deregulation, buried inspection waivers, and quiet NAY votes on bills threatening his clients.
rolodex.watchOut: Holds the keys to your campaign War Chest—helpful against attack ads, dangerous if the Ethics Board starts auditing.

pig.name: Rep. Wilbur Troughman
pig.visualBrief: Portly pink-and-cream veteran lawmaker in a burgundy three-piece waistcoat, brass suspenders, handlebar tusks, waving a gold fountain pen.

rolodex.whatTheyWant: Earmarks, concrete contracts, and old-fashioned vote trading ('you back my project, I'll back yours').
rolodex.watchOut: His riders look ugly on paper, yet occasionally bring real local jobs—and his Favor token can save your Flagship Bill.

bear.name: Chairwoman Beatrice Kodiak
bear.visualBrief: Imposing brown bear in a structured tweed blazer, tortoiseshell spectacles, pearl pin, resting one paw on a massive oak gavel.

rolodex.whatTheyWant: Institutional integrity, thorough reading of redacted clauses, and lawmakers with spine.
rolodex.watchOut: Never try to haggle with her—earn her respect by exposing hidden ink, and her Election Night endorsement swings votes.

bird.name: Mags Magpie
bird.visualBrief: Sharp black-and-white magpie in a belted trench coat, tilted fedora with a 'PRESS' card tucked in the band, vintage flash-bulb camera.

rolodex.office: Capitol Press Gallery (Staking Out the Coatroom)
rolodex.whatTheyWant: Scandals, contradictions, and six-second hallway soundbites that sell morning papers.
rolodex.watchOut: When her flash bulb pops after major omnibus votes, you only get 6 seconds to pick a spin matching your actual vote!

fox.name: Sterling Foxworth
fox.visualBrief: Impossibly polished russet fox with focus-grouped coiffed fur, tailored navy blazer over cream turtleneck, blinding campaign smile.

rolodex.whatTheyWant: Your congressional seat—and any awkward vote he can splice into a 30-second prime-time attack ad.
rolodex.watchOut: Once he enters the race in Week 7, running low on War Chest funds lets his unanswered billboards drain every Maple Creek bloc weekly.

constituentPostcards.sender: Mrs. Lupine (Wolf), 3rd-Grade Teacher — Maple Creek Elementary
constituentPostcards.note: Parents are begging for bright lamps by the school bus stop—though I heard retired folks on Oak Street are worried about how the town will pay for it!

constituentPostcards.sender: Sal Viper (Snake), Owner — Main Street Sourdough Bakery
constituentPostcards.note: Folks are split down here, Barnaby! Families want the free river bridge and strict runoff rules, but riverside workshops say new compliance fees could squeeze them dry.

constituentPostcards.sender: Sal Viper & Hector Badger — Maple Creek Merchants
constituentPostcards.note: Heads up: Main Street is desperate for foot traffic and the 150 jobs in today's Rail Depot bill. Even if Troughman stuffed ugly pork in it, downtown shops WANT this passed!

constituentPostcards.sender: Old Man Boarwell (Pig), Retired Postal Carrier
constituentPostcards.note: Online shops love cheaper bulk shipping, sure—but check the blacked-out lines on today's Post Office bill! Seniors depend on our walk-in counter for prescriptions.

constituentPostcards.sender: Mrs. Lupine & Penny Mallard — Joint Maple Creek Note
constituentPostcards.note: Downtown shops really need those storm loans and seniors need ambulance upgrades, Barnaby—just PLEASE read Page 3 before deciding what they're trading away!

constituentPostcards.sender: Martha Ewe (Sheep) — Maple Creek Town Hall
constituentPostcards.note: Your Flagship Bill hits the floor today! Maple Creek is watching to see if you pass it clean, trade favors, or stuff someone else's earmark into your own promise.

constituentPostcards.sender: Dr. Oona Owl (Owl), High School Civics Teacher
constituentPostcards.note: We tried diagramming H.R. 615 on the chalkboard and broke three pieces of chalk. Read your Staff Legal Memo—and watch out for that slick new Fox on our billboards!

constituentPostcards.sender: Sal Viper & Coach Bruno Bear — Maple Creek Diner
constituentPostcards.note: Foxworth's glossy ads are everywhere! Careful with today's 'Ethics' bill—rumor says the redacted fine print slaps huge audit fees on local chamber mixers and potlucks.

constituentPostcards.sender: Old Man Boarwell (Pig) — Maple Creek Watchdogs
constituentPostcards.note: Delivery trucks are furious about the Highway 9 bridge detour, so Main Street wants a fast AYE—but Chairwoman Kodiak warned us Page 3 hides 75-year no-bid contracts!
Polls open at sunrise! Tonight's midnight bill freezes senior property taxes—but rumor says an 11:58 PM rider slashes school buses and small-shop grants to pay for it.

archetypes.title: The Neighborhood Reformer
archetypes.tagline: "Read the fine print, listen to Maple Creek, owe nobody."
archetypes.description: Strong start with Families and Seniors, modest ties with Main Street, and a shoestring War Chest that Leadership eyes warily.

archetypes.title: The Coalition Builder
archetypes.tagline: "Nobody wins Washington alone—find the middle lane."
archetypes.description: Balanced standing across all three Maple Creek blocs, solid Caucus ties, and enough cash to stay nimble.

archetypes.title: The Main Street Booster
archetypes.tagline: "Bring jobs and projects home first; argue details later."
archetypes.description: Beloved by Main Street merchants with a flush War Chest, though Families and Seniors keep a sharp eye on your receipts.

endings.title: SUBPOENAED BEFORE THE CONFETTI DROPS
endings.headline: BREAKING: ETHICS BOARD RAIDS BARKER VICTORY PARTY OVER 'MYSTERY ESPRESSO MACHINE'
endings.subhead: You played the backroom game recklessly and got sloppy on camera—even K-Street is shredding your phone number.
endings.epilogue: Mags Magpie wins a national journalism award for printing your sticky-note trail. Whip Fang issues a three-word statement: 'Barely met him.'

endings.title: THE ACCIDENTAL SPEAKER
endings.headline: SHOCK ON CAPITOL HILL: FRESHMAN BARKER UNANIMOUSLY DRAFTED AS SPEAKER!
endings.subhead: Zero broken promises, broad Maple Creek support, a passed Flagship Bill, and Kodiak's seal—you pulled off the rarest feat in Congress.
endings.epilogue: Pundits spend months wondering how a wide-eyed rookie unified Families, Seniors, Main Street, and the Caucus without selling out.

endings.title: THE HOMETOWN COALITION CHAMPION
endings.headline: MR. BARKER GOES BACK TO WASHINGTON! MAPLE CREEK VOTERS DEFY THE MACHINE!
endings.subhead: With low corruption and a rock-solid hometown coalition, you proved a freshman can win by keeping a finger on the local pulse.
endings.epilogue: Sal Viper brings cinnamon rolls, Mrs. Lupine's class sends banners, and Whip Fang quietly moves your desk away from the radiator.

endings.title: MASTER OF THE MACHINE
endings.headline: MAPLE CREEK BAFFLED AS BARKER WINS REELECTION ON 40,000 GLOSSY ATTACK ADS
endings.subhead: Half your hometown blocs were fuming, but disciplined press spin, donor cash, and party muscle carried you across 50%.
endings.epilogue: Your desk is solid mahogany now. You still keep Mrs. Lupine's faded class card in a drawer—right behind the velvet briefcase.

endings.title: THE UNPREDICTABLE COALITION BUILDER
endings.headline: SPLIT TICKET SHOCKER: NOBODY KNOWS WHAT BARKER WILL DO NEXT—AND VOTERS CAN'T LOOK AWAY!
endings.subhead: You traded votes, stitched together an unlikely Maple Creek coalition, and survived by keeping every faction guessing.
endings.epilogue: Columnists spend all winter debating whether you're a principled independent or a sly horse-trader. Even Toby Otter isn't totally sure.

endings.title: ONE-TERM IDEALIST
endings.headline: TOO CLEAN FOR THE AIRWAVES? BARKER LOSES SEAT DESPITE HOMETOWN GOODWILL
endings.subhead: Your integrity stayed spotless, but an empty War Chest and cold Caucus ties let Sterling Foxworth own every billboard in Maple Creek.
endings.epilogue: You head home with your tail high, a standing ovation at the diner, and a hit civics podcast called 'Wait, Did You Read Page 1,204?'

endings.title: OUT-FOXED AT THE POLLS
endings.headline: PRIMARY UPSET! STERLING FOXWORTH SWEEPS MAPLE CREEK AS BARKER COALITION FRACTURES
endings.subhead: Caught between split local blocs and vengeful Capitol insiders, your winning coalition collapsed before Election Night.
endings.epilogue: Within 48 hours, Vesper Viper slips an embossed business card under your door: 'Need a consulting gig, kid? Former reps make wonderful lobbyists.'

civicReceipts.summary: No representative's district agrees on everything: families, retirees, and local businesses often have genuinely competing interests on the exact same bill, forcing lawmakers to build workable coalitions rather than chasing 100% approval.
Controversial funding offsets or policy riders are routinely attached to popular bills right before a vote, forcing lawmakers to weigh real local benefits against painful fine print.
Combining hundreds of unrelated measures into one giant must-pass bill squeezes out amendment debate and guarantees critics can attack whichever way a representative votes.
Passing a signature bill often requires adding targeted funding or concessions for colleagues' priorities—trading legislative purity to build a working floor majority.
Procedural motions and ballot phrasing are sometimes written in nested negatives so that voting 'Aye' achieves the opposite of what the friendly title suggests.

civicReceipts.term: Caucus Whips, Ad Wars & Primary Challengers
civicReceipts.summary: Leadership enforces discipline via committee assignments and endorsements, while running out of campaign funds leaves even popular lawmakers vulnerable to unanswered primary attack ads.
Complex legislative trade-offs rarely fit in a six-second hallway clip, rewarding lawmakers who frame their votes quickly before opponents define them first.
